subject: DPA: data sovereignty & deletion window — redlines and next steps
body:
From: Anna Schultz <anna@heliosanalytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Helios Analytics Legal <legal@heliosanalytics.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA: data residency and deletion windows — initial redlines & questions

Karthik,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier this week. I attached our initial redlines to the standard DPA (DPA_redlines_helios_v1.docx) — the core asks from our side:

- EU-only processing for personal data of EU residents (including backups and logs).
- Ability to require deletion of subject data within 45 calendar days of a verified request (including any copies held by sub-processors).
- Retention carve-out: aggregated analytics (non-identifiable) may be retained for up to 24 months but must be demonstrably non-reversible.
- Right to audit / receive deletion verification logs and an updated sub-processor list with region details.

We assume Redwood offers a hosted API; please confirm whether you can commit to EU-only storage/processing for Helios EU users under the hosted plan, or whether this requires Dedicated/Private deployment. Also confirm whether you can meet the 45-day deletion window, and whether deletion verification logs are available for export.

Anna
Lead Counsel | Helios Analytics
anna@heliosanalytics.com
Attachment: DPA_redlines_helios_v1.docx (docx)

Subject: Re: DPA: data residency and deletion windows — initial redlines & questions

Anna — thanks for the redlines and the clear summary. Quick responses below, and we attached a short response doc with suggested compromise language (redwood_response_dpa_20260411.docx).

High level: Redwood supports multiple deployment options with different levels of control over geography and deletion guarantees. The options and practical implications:

1) Hosted API (standard): global routing by default. We do not currently offer a unilateral EU-only processing guarantee on the standard hosted plan because requests can be routed to any region for performance and capacity reasons. We do, however, provide data partitioning and encryption, and we can include a contractual commitment to use EU region for processing in many cases, but it is contingent on capacity and sub-processor constraints.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) / Region-pinning: Dedicated pools can be provisioned in a specific cloud region (e.g., eu-west-1). This is the recommended path to get an operational EU-only guarantee for both active tokens and KV/prefix caches. It does require a committed capacity contract.

3) Private (VPC/on-prem): full control — we can guarantee EU-only processing and handle deletion to your specifications; this is the cleanest option for strict data-sovereignty requirements.

Deletion windows: our default hosted deletion SLA is 90 days for full propagation across backups and sub-processors. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can support 45-day deletion and, in specific designs, 30-day deletion with an agreed operational playbook (additional engineering verification). Meeting 45 days for hosted customers is possible but operationally risky without region control.

Verification: we can provide deletion logs and a certificate of deletion export for Dedicated/Private customers. For hosted customers we can provide event logs but cannot guarantee sub-processor-internal deletion timing unless sub-processors are EU-only.

Next steps: 1) Marissa (legal) and Neha (security) are cc'd to propose contractual language and confirm technical requirements. 2) Can we schedule a 30-minute call early next week to walk the redlines and expected timeline? I can propose Tue/Wed.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood_response_dpa_20260411.docx (docx)

Subject: Re: DPA: data residency and deletion windows — initial redlines & questions

Hi Anna — following on Karthik's note. I reviewed the redlines and sketched some pragmatic DPA language that should be acceptable to both sides; attaching a short PDF with clause suggestions (DPA_clause_suggestions.pdf). High-level suggestions: 

- Data residency clause: replace absolute "EU-only" phrasing with: 
  "Redwood will process personal data relating to EU Residents in data centers located in the European Economic Area (EEA) for the term of the Agreement, except for temporary failover events where processing may occur outside the EEA for up to 72 hours. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to ensure sub-processors maintain EEA-only processing for Helios-designated datasets."

- Deletion window: propose a two-tier approach in the DPA: 
  * Hosted: "Redwood will permanently delete personal data in its active datasets within ninety (90) days of a verified deletion request and will use commercially reasonable efforts to remove backups and caches within an additional ninety (90) days."
  * Dedicated/Private: "Redwood will permanently delete personal data within forty-five (45) days and provide an exportable deletion verification report within ten (10) days after deletion is completed."

- Audit/verification: include a clause allowing one annual audit (remote or on-site with reasonable notice) for Dedicated/Private customers and an obligation to provide deletion logs and sub-processor region lists on request for hosted customers.

If Helios needs a strict 45-day SLA for all customers, we need to surface this as a contractual exception that will require either Dedicated capacity or Private deployment and a commercial uplift to cover engineering and sub-processor tooling.

Operational/technical notes for Neha: we will need to document the sub-processor list by region and confirm backup retention architecture for the relevant dataset. Neha — can you prepare the current sub-processor map and expected RTO for backups by Mon EOD?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Attachment: DPA_clause_suggestions.pdf (pdf)

Thanks, Marissa and Karthik — that language is helpful and closer to what we need. A few follow-ups before we circulate to procurement: 

1) Timeline: can you confirm how long it will take to produce the deletion verification report for Dedicated customers (you suggested 10 days after deletion) — we need that in the SOW.
2) Audit artifacts: please share existing SOC 2 report and any ISO attestations you have, plus the current sub-processor-by-region spreadsheet (redacted where needed).
3) We want to block the Hosted fallback option for EU datasets — i.e., if Helios designates a dataset as "EU-resident" we need a contractual commitment that Redwood will not route or process that dataset outside EEA except for documented emergency failover. That language may be acceptable with an explicit emergency carve-out and notice timelines.

If you can provide the SOC 2 and sub-processor map this week and confirm timeline for the deletion report and a proposed SOW paragraph for Dedicated capacity (including estimated uplift), we'll route to procurement (deal id HLX-2026-042) and aim to sign within two weeks.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — let's tentatively book Tue 14 Apr 2026 at 09:00 CET for a 30-min call; Karthik — can you send a calendar invite?

Anna Schultz
